notes.title: Demo updated to 0.8.1.4: TEETH
notes.content:
Main Content: SCP-127

During development, we have gone back and forth on the inclusion of a weapon in the game. From the [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VMF8DTFr-vc]Original trailer[/url] of the game to several updates along the way, we have experimented with different ways for the player to defend themselves. Not against anomalies—never against the anomalies—but against the other monsters of the game: people.

In many playtests and even the original teaser released in January of this year, D-974 was entirely unarmed. But the goal was never to be defenseless. The weapon, or weapons, given to the player must be useful, require management of a precious resource, and ideally be an existing SCP.

Our version of SCP-127 is a bit different from the [url=https://scp-wiki.wikidot.com/scp-127]original written by far2[/url]. Instead of regrowing teeth, D-974 must harvest this previous ammunition from the environment: from corpses of dead Foundation agents littering the facility and from GOC operatives he takes down.

But teeth are a precious commodity. Use the bullets sparingly, or you might find yourself running out when you need them most.

notes.title: Infohazard Demo patch 0.8.1
notes.content:
[b]Patch Notes - Version 0.8.1[/b]

We've just pushed a shiny new bugfix patch, and boy, do we have some fun updates for you. Check out what's new below:

[list]
[*]Fixed an issue with ground detection allowing the player to double-jump. 
[*]Fixed an issue that made it hard to ascend stairs.
[*]Fed Jeffery. 
[*]Removed some debug graphics from the UI that weren't supposed to show. 
[*]Fixed a couple of dialogue lines. 
[*]Added some additional optimizations to the game's screen effects so they run smoother. 
[*]Fixed several menu items that would not function. 
[*]Fixed a bug that prevented quitting the game from the main menu. You can now escape. [i] Or can you...?[/i]
[*]Altered the player's movement speed slightly. 
[*]Fixed several other minor bugs. 
[/list]

Thanks for your continued support and feedback! Keep exploring, keep surviving, and don't forget to feed Jeffery!

notes.title: Official Trailer for SCP: Infohazard released
notes.content:
[b][url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VMF8DTFr-vc]Check out the trailer here![/url][/b]

[b]Release Date: March 1, 2024[/b]

We just released the official trailer on March 1 to announce [i]SCP: Infohazard[/i], an adventure horror game, the latest in several pieces of media taking place in the universe of the fictional SCP Foundation. 

The trailer for Infohazard showcases incredible detail and aesthetic, as well as a retro-noir feel & appearance which is often likened to modern titles like Lethal Company. The Foundation’s ruling shadow council, the O5s, are shown, along with several highly-detailed locations, including a darkened containment facility, a disturbing mansion, and a lone phone booth on an otherworldly landscape. 
The trailer comes on the heels of the demo for Infohazard released on Steam at the beginning of the year. This 5-minute demo showcases the dread-inducing aesthetic of Site-97 by highlighting three separate parts of the facility.

[i]SCP: Infohazard[/i] aims to be funded by its Kickstarter which launches this fall. Its initial goal of $50,000 is only the beginning, as the team hopes to raise upwards of $250,000 to produce a real “AAA SCP experience.” According to the team, the game will be released in chapters to reduce development time and costs, following a model popularized by titles such as Bendy and the Ink Machine.

In [i]Infohazard[/i], the player takes the role of a foundation test subject, utilized by the mysterious Foundation to help deal with the most dangerous monsters and anomalies that they contain. The player must navigate through the high-tech facility and neutralize reality-destroying anomalies—using their wits, rather than weapons, against the creatures in their way.

“We wanted to create an SCP game that was more than just shooting monsters,” said GIB Games CEO Sam Swicegood, “This game immerses the player and lets them explore the details of the facility in new and unique ways.” Swicegood has been a writer for the SCP Wiki for over a decade, and is an award-winning sci-fi and fantasy author—his titles include the 2018 Wizards on Walnut Street and 2019 New Apple Literary Award winner No Place.

The SCP Foundation is a massive collaborative project that began in 2008. This open-source fiction setting comprises tens of thousands of collaborative derivative works. The open properties of the license allow it to be utilized by indie development studios for games, movies, and other works, such as the popular SCP: Containment Breach published by Undertow Games in 2012. The SCP Foundation universe has a community of millions of fans. 

"The SCP community has created thousands of amazing creative works," said Sherman Christensen, creator of [url=https://www.tiktok.com/@site_42]Site-42[/url], which has amassed over 3 million followers across multiple platforms, "Infohazard is full of details that hardcore SCP fans will love—while still being a fun and immersive adventure for people new to The Foundation." Christensen is one of several SCP content creators working with GIB Games in the development of this project. Others include well-known members of the SCP community including [url=https://www.tiktok.com/@desk.of.alto.clef]The Desk of Alto Clef[/url] and [url=https://www.tiktok.com/@mayorlovecraft]Mayor Lovecraft[/url]—aka Leeman Kessler, the real-life mayor of Gambier, Ohio and horror enthusiast.

The team behind Infohazard promise that the game will be chock-full of community favorite anomalies such as SCP-999. “We even have plushies as a kickstarter add-on,” Swicegood added with a laugh. Other anomalies confirmed to be in SCP:Infohazard include SCP-096, SCP-682, SCP-3930, and SCP-3008.

The SCP: Infohazard project can be followed at [url=https://scp.game]scp.game[/url]

notes.title: Infohazard is coming to Desktop
notes.content:
Since the announcement of [i]SCP:Infohazard[/i] we have gotten a lot of questions about the content, playstyle, and more. One of the biggest responses is always "I wish I had VR so I could play this" or "Is it coming to desktop?"

We heard you. And we want to share the awesome [i]Infohazard[/i] experience with all of you. So we've come to a decision: [b]Infohazard will be developed with cross-play in mind.[/b]

This will be a bit of a change. Like our previous VR titles, we approached the development of the game with solely VR in mind. And while we still want to make sure the VR experience is super immersive and as amazing as possible, we will be developing the flat-screen experience alongside it.

Some VR things don't translate well to flat-screen, though. What this means is that non-VR users are likely going to have some tangible changes in the experience—things like object manipulation and weapons will be handled completely differently. So, because of that, we are going to recommend that this game be played in VR if possible. But we're going to do everything we can to make the desktop experience just as fun.

-Toast

notes.title: GIB Games announces "SCP: Infohazard"
notes.content:
Hey there, SCP fans! GIB Games is pleased to announce SCP: Infohazard, an adventure horror experience playable in VR.

In Infohazard, the player takes the role of a prisoner on death row, utilized by the mysterious SCP Foundation to help deal with the most dangerous monsters and anomalies that they contain. The player must navigate through the high-tech facility, often diverting into other well-known and established locations.

The trailer for Infohazard showcases the incredible aesthetics we're known for at GIB. In just 30 seconds, several highly-detailed locations are shown, including a darkened containment facility, a disturbing mansion, and a lone phone booth on an otherworldly landscape.

We wanted to create an SCP game that was more than just shooting monsters. We want this game to immerse the player and let them explore the details of the facility in new and unique ways.

For those of you unfamiliar: the SCP Foundation is a massive collaborative project that began in 2008. This open-source fiction setting comprises tens of thousands of collaborative derivative works, most of which originate on the SCP Foundation Wiki. The open properties of the license allow it to be utilized by indie development studios for games, movies, and other works, such as the popular SCP: Containment Breach published by Undertow Games in 2012. The SCP Foundation universe has a community of hundreds of thousands of fans.

Infohazard is full of details that hardcore SCP fans will love—while still being a fun and immersive adventure for people new to The Foundation.
